evidence: checkpoint.lisp:453-463 `(fnn-mkdir stage #o700) (fnn-write-staged ...) ... (fnn-clone-copy-tree source-real stage 0 max-depth max-entries max-bytes path-bound)` runs before checkpoint.lisp:255-258 `#-linux ... (fnn-refuse "clone publication requires no-replace renameat2")`. No unwind-protect removes `stage` on any refusal or fault (byte, entry or depth bound exceeded, destination appeared, copy error).
fix: Check publication support (the platform and a RENAME_NOREPLACE probe) before mkdir. Wrap the copy in an unwind-protect that removes the stage tree on a definite refusal or fault, keeping it only when the publication outcome is indeterminate.
reviewer: checkpoint.lisp:453-463 creates the stage directory, writes the fence and copies the whole tree before fnn-clone-publish-no-replace. Off Linux that function unconditionally refuses (checkpoint.lisp:255-258). No unwind-protect or handler removes stage on any refusal or fault: copy bounds, destination appeared, or publish. No code elsewhere references the .fn-clone- prefix (grep finds only checkpoint.lisp:438), and clone-resume takes only DESTINATION. Each failed attempt on OpenBSD/Darwin therefore leaves a full copy. It is an operator-invoked verb and the refusal is visible.
scenario: On the OpenBSD friend node or on Darwin, `checkpoint clone SRC DST` copies up to fn-store-checkpoint-clone-max-bytes into `.fn-clone-<pid>-<hex>` and is then refused, leaving a full copy beside the store. Each retry leaves another. On Linux, a copy refused for exceeding the byte bound leaves its partial stage behind the same way. There is no verb that finds or removes these stage directories.
title: Clone copies the whole store before learning publication is impossible off Linux, and a failed clone never removes its stage directory
